text:
maya: bringing up user/lilac-7b on Redwood convert, hitting a hard failure during load: AutoConfigError: Could not find class 'LilacConfig' in model files. conversion aborted.

jon: did you try loading with trust_remote_code=True locally? many of these community models have custom config/classes.

maya: yeah tried `from_pretrained(..., trust_remote_code=True)` and it loads locally, but redwood convert rejects the package unless we embed an auto_map entry. also worried about security.

jon: quick checklist: 1) check `config.json` for `auto_map`, 2) confirm tokenizer files include special tokens, 3) avoid unsafe remote execution unless reviewed. example `auto_map` snippet we added to downstream pack:
```json
"auto_map": {
  "AutoConfig": "lilac.modeling_lilac.LilacConfig",
  "AutoModelForCausalLM": "lilac.modeling_lilac.LilacForCausalLM"
}
```

sam: small gotcha: even after adding auto_map, Redwood runtime crashed in generation because `generation_config.pad_token_id` was None. the model's tokenizer didn't declare pad/eos/bos in `tokenizer_config.json`. Reducing batch size also surfaced different tokenization behavior in chat templates.

maya: exact error from redwood runtime: `ValueError: pad_token_id is None. please set pad_token_id on the tokenizer or in generation config` — stacktrace points to `generate()` path after quantized conversion.

alex: this lines up with quantization experiments we ran: some 4-bit quant packs merged embeddings and the tokenizer->vocab mapping got subtly shifted, causing off-by-one token ids for special tokens. end-to-end eval showed hallucination uptick.

eval-bot: quick eval summary: baseline fp16 -> dev_chat_qa EM=72.3, quant 4bit-> EM=60.8 (drop 11.5). perplexity increased on heldout prompts with system messages.

sam: pragmatic workaround we used: (1) vendor adds explicit `special_tokens_map` in `tokenizer_config.json` including pad_token/pad_token_id, (2) add `modeling_adapter.py` that subclasses and maps `forward(*args, **kwargs)` to standard signature, so we can avoid trust_remote_code at runtime.

jon: another path: add a small redwood-side `redwood_model_config.json` shipped alongside model with whitelisted auto_map mapping + sha256 of files. then conversion tool runs in a review mode and accepts the mapping without enabling arbitrary remote code execution.

maya: commands we used locally for repro: 
```bash
# load with remote code to inspect classes
python -c "from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM; m=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('user/lilac-7b', trust_remote_code=True); print(type(m))"
# convert for redwood with explicit flags (internal dev tool)
redwood convert ./user_lilac7b --include-tokenizer-config --whitelist-auto-map ./redwood_model_config.json --skip-sanity=false
```

alex: note: if you must quantize, run the token-level eval after quantization with the same chat templates used in production. the tokenizer special tokens being missing will mostly show up when system prompts are prepended (prefix caching interacts badly with missing eos/pad).

infra-bot: conversion tool tip: add `--require-tokenizer-specials` to block converts that don't define pad/eos/bos. filing an internal ticket to flip that flag on by default.

maya: action items: 1) ask model author for `auto_map` + explicit tokenizer_config, 2) run adapter to standardize forward signatures (sam to prototype), 3) run quantized eval suite (alex + eval-bot) and compare pre/post.

sam: I'll prototype the adapter and push a minimal example to `eng-ml/examples/lilac_adapter` — will share followup. :thumbsup:

jon: +1, and let's add a short doc on our conversion checklist (trust_remote_code implications, auto_map, tokenizer specials, quant eval) so PMs/sales know the lift.
